text:
alert-bot: ALERT firing: prometheus_remote_write_queue_length > 1000 (us-west-2). remote_write errors spiking, retries++ :warning:

eva: seeing big backlog on prometheus-us-west. remote_write to thanos-recv-us-west returning 5xx and timeouts. grafana shows queue length jump at 10:12 UTC.

sam: yup, retries_total and remote_write_send_failures spiked. latency for remote_write_send_seconds p95 went from 200ms -> 2.1s.

priya: any config changes in the last deploy window?

sam: we pushed a new kube-state-metrics sidecar yesterday to all clusters. suspiciously around the same time.

priya: pulling prometheus logs from the pod now. tail:
```
level=error ts=2026-03-18T10:12:34.123Z caller=queue_manager.go:238 component=remote_write err="error sending samples: context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
metrics_count=834712
```

eva: whoa. also noticing a cardinality blip in Grafana: unique series count on scrape target kube-state-metrics jumped 4x. looks like a label with container id or full pod name got added.

sam: config diff shows kube-state-metrics started exposing label pod_name_full which contains the pod UID suffix. that's likely creating ephemeral series.

priya: confirmed in the scrape target: ``pod_name_full: my-app-6f8b7d9c-7x2l9`` which changes every pod restart. bad.

sam: immediate mitigation: drop that label in Prometheus relabel_config. propose patch:
```
- job_name: 'kube-state-metrics'
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['10.0.3.12:8080']
  relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: ['pod_name_full']
    action: 'drop'
```
This will prevent series explosion.

eva: better to also normalize pod label so dashboards that rely on pod_name still work. suggestion: extract prefix before first '-' and keep short pod base name instead:```
- action: replace
  source_labels: ["pod_name_full"]
  target_label: "pod_name"
  regex: "([a-z0-9-]+)-[a-z0-9]+$"
  replacement: "$1"
```
That will turn my-app-6f8b7d9c-7x2l9 -> my-app.

marc: note: even after relabeling the backlog, remote_write queue might still be clogged because of max_shards/capacity config. we should bump queue_config on prometheus specifically for us-west so it drains faster and avoid throttling in thanos-recv. e.g.:
```
remote_write:
- url: https://thanos-recv-us-west.internal:19291/api/v1/receive
  queue_config:
    max_shards: 200
    capacity: 25000
    max_samples_per_send: 1000
```
But this increases memory. tradeoff vs dropping data.

priya: agree. we should do relabel drop first to stop new cardinality then increase queue capacity briefly to let backlog drain. also check egress limits for the region. us-west-2 has 5Gbps cap on the instance fleet and we might be saturating it.

eva: I'm going to apply the relabel drop to prometheus-us-west configmap (canary) and POST /-/reload to avoid full restart. command:
```
kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prometheus-us-west --patch '...'
# then
kubectl -n monitoring exec deploy/prometheus-us-west -c prometheus -- curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9090/-/reload
```
I'll watch queue length and series count.

sam: if POST reload doesn't pick up for some reason we can force-roll the statefulset.

priya: also add a relabel to drop any label matching "pod_name_full" globally across kube-state-metrics scrape jobs. easier to revert.

marc: reminder: after drain, we should adjust alert thresholds to account for transient spikes and add a panel that breaks down series growth by label key so we can pinpoint future label-inflicted cardinality.

eva: patch applied in us-west. reload returned 200. watching...

(5m pass)

eva: queue_length dropping from 1200 -> 80. unique_series for kube-state-metrics down to normal. remote_write_send_failures trending to zero. :tada:

alert-bot: RESOLVED: prometheus_remote_write_queue_length (prometheus-us-west) back to normal.

sam: tracked root cause: kube-state-metrics sidecar added pod_name_full label. follow-up: send a PR to kube-state-metrics helm values to stop exporting that label, and add an ops playbook for immediate relabeling steps.

priya: i'll open the PR and a short runbook. tagging @eng-ml and @devex to confirm dashboards that reference pod_name still behave.

marc: also create a small job to run promtool check-config and simulate relabel impacts in staging before rolling to prod.

eva: nice work team. lessons: (1) drop noisy labels fast, (2) watch queue config for temporary scale, (3) watch egress caps per region.

sam: adding links to the runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/prometheus-cardinality.md and grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/abcd1234/remote-write-ops

priya: closing the thread once PRs and runbook are in.
